note: Exemplar selections for the seventeen public-domain writing styles. Each key addresses a verbatim passage in that style's own corpus, resolved by exemplar_lib.by_key. The annotation is ours and describes the construction; the passage is never touched.

austen-novels: the narration slides into the character's own words and keeps the judgement she is passing on herself
a refusal delivered inside the forms of politeness, the sting carried by the courtesy
faraday-lectures: the demonstration is described as it happens in front of the audience, with the apparatus pointed at
a proportion stated, then the weights that establish it
pepys-diary: the day taken in order from rising to bed, business and appetite given the same weight
the parenthesis carries the household business while the main clause keeps going
chesterfield-letters: advice issued as an allowance of hours, with the reason attached to it
approval, then a correction, then the letter closes on one word
beeton-household-manual: the method runs as a single imperative sequence with the timings inside it
quantities first, then the order of work, then how long it stands
post-etiquette: a rule established through a named example and a line quoted from her
the custom stated, then the tradition it rests on
strunk-style-manual: the principle is stated once, then examples are set against it one at a time
an instruction that names the fault it is correcting before it gives the remedy
aurelius-meditations-casaubon: numbered addresses to himself, each finished within a sentence or two
an analogy opens the entry and the whole argument is carried out inside it
grimm-fairy-tales-taylor: the opening formula sets the household and its imbalance in three sentences
speech reported in full, with the bargain spoken aloud by both sides
twain-travel-letters: the solemn cadence is built up and then spent on the trivial object
a portrait assembled from two habits held together in one sentence
darwin-voyage-journal: the date is given, then the conditions, then what was counted
a process followed step by step in the order it was watched
white-selborne-letters: an observation reported to a correspondent, with the watcher's own care described
a claim about numbers, then the enquiry standing behind it
dana-sea-narrative: the crew's speech carries the working of the ship
the work ahead listed in the order it will be done
slocum-voyage-narrative: the chase told in the order it happened, the hailed word kept as it was spoken
the port's kindness itemised, then the evening in one sentence
field-notes: the entry opens on its date and the object of the day's work
an accident of digging is followed until it yields an identification
ships-log: the call goes up and the watch's gear is listed as it is put away
distance run, then the weather, then the anchorage
aphorism: each numbered claim is general and stops as soon as it is complete
the run alternates lengths so a short maxim lands against a longer one
